title: Learning-Augmented Approximation for Unrelated-Machines Makespan Scheduling
claim: Accurate predictions give near-optimal results that degrade gracefully with error and stay within the worst-case bound, with negligible runtime.
layout: 3 panels side by side, shared legend style, dashed baseline line, shaded error bands
description: Three line plots in a row. Panels (a) and (b) show makespan ratio C_max(S)/OPT on the y-axis against false-negative rate and false-positive rate of the predictions on the x-axis. Three curves for Ours with K=0, 1 and 2 (blue circles, orange squares, pink triangles) have shaded standard-error bands. A green dashed horizontal line marks the LST 2-approximation baseline at the top. In (a), the curves start at 1.0 and rise slowly, and larger K stays lower. In (b), all three curves rise steeply and saturate at the LST line near 0.4. Panel (c) plots runtime in seconds against the number of machines m from 2 to 10. LST (1+ε) and Mordechai+LST outer curves blow up, while Ours and LST 2-approx stay flat near zero. Each panel has a legend.
caption: Numerical results. (a) and (b) show the change in makespan as the false-negative and false-positive rates are varied, respectively. (c) shows the change in running time as the number of machines \(m\) is varied; the curves for Ours with \(K=0,1,2\) and the LST \(2\)-approximation baseline overlap because they finish almost immediately. The lines denote the mean, and the shaded regions denote the standard error, both computed over 30 independent runs with different random seeds.
abstract: Recently, Antoniadis et al. (ICLR 2025) proposed a framework for incorporating predictions to approximate NP-hard selection problems. Despite its simplicity, this approach tightly matches theoretical lower bounds, making its generalization highly compelling. We address an open question raised in the work of Antoniadis et al., concerning the extension of this approach to other important problems outside the class of selection problems, such as scheduling. We develop a learning-augmented algorithm for the makespan minimization problem on unrelated machines, denoted by $R\|C_{\max}$. By using predictions of heavy job assignments, we achieve a polynomial-time $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation for accurate predictions that smoothly degrades to a worst-case 2-approximation as the error increases. We conclude our work with an empirical analysis of our method.
